We calculate the derivative using the quotient rule, as follows:

\begin{align} f'(x) &= \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(\dfrac {5-2\csc x}{e^x }\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {(2\csc x \cot x)e^x - (5-2\csc x)e^x }{(e^x)^2 } \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {e^x(2\csc x \cot x-5+2\csc x) }{e^{2x} } \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {2\csc x \cot x+2\csc x -5 }{e^{x} } \end{align}

exampleAnswers.title: Differentiating Expressions Involving the Cotangent Function

question.explanation:
First, we just take the constant out of the derivative and use the result for the derivative of $\cot x,$ as follows: \begin{eqnarray} \eqalign{ f'(x) & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( -6\cot x\right) \\[5pt] & =- 6(-\csc^2 x) \\[5pt] & =6 \csc^2 x } \end{eqnarray}

Then, we substitute $x=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ in the derivative and get \begin{align} f'\left(\dfrac \pi 6\right) & = 6 \csc^2 \left(\dfrac \pi 6\right)\\[5pt] & =6\left( 2\right)^2 \\[5pt] & = 24. \end{align}

exampleAnswers.title: Differentiating Expressions Involving the Secant Function

question.text: Find the derivative of $y = 4\sec{x} + e^{x}$ at $x=0.$
question.explanation:
First, we take the derivative of each term and then add them:

\begin{align*} \dfrac {\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} &= \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\!\left(4\sec{x} + e^{x}\right) \\[5pt] &= 4\sec{x}\tan{x} + e^{x} \end{align*}

Then, we substitute $x = 0$:

\begin{align*} \dfrac {\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}\Bigg|_{x=0} &=(4\sec{x}\tan{x} + e^{x})\,\Bigg|_{x=0} \\[5pt] &= 4\sec{(0)}\tan{(0)} + e^{0} \\[5pt] &= 4\cdot1\cdot0 + 1 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{1} \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Slope of the Tangent at a Point of a Function Involving Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions

question.text: Find the slope of $y=f(x)$ at $x = \sqrt 3$ if $f(x) = 11\cos x - \sec x + \dfrac 1 x.$
question.explanation:
First, we calculate the derivative using the sum rule:

\begin{eqnarray} \eqalign{ f'(x) &= \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(11\cos x - \sec x + \dfrac 1 x \right) \\ &= \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(11\cos x - \sec x + x^{-1}\right) \\ & = 11(-\sin x) - \sec x \tan x - \dfrac 1{x^2} \\ & = -11\sin x -\sec x \tan x -\dfrac 1{x^2} } \end{eqnarray}

Then, we substitute $x=\sqrt 3$ in the derivative and get \begin{align} f'(\sqrt 3) & = -11\sin( \sqrt 3) -\sec ( \sqrt 3) \tan( \sqrt 3) - \dfrac{1}{(\sqrt 3)^2}\\[3pt] & =-11\sin( \sqrt 3) -\sec ( \sqrt 3) \tan( \sqrt 3) - \dfrac 1 3. \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Slope of the Tangent at a Point of a Function Involving Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions

question.text: Find the slope $m$ of $y=g(x)$ at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ if $g(x) = -4e^x\csc x + 6.$
question.explanation:
First, we calculate the derivative using the product rule and sum rule:

\begin{align*} g'(x) &=\dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\!\left(-4e^x\csc x + 6\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{d}{dx}(-4e^x)\cdot \csc x + (-4e^x)\cdot \dfrac{d}{dx}(\csc x) + \dfrac{d}{dx}(6) \\[5pt] &= -4e^x\csc x + (-4e^x)(- \csc x \cot x) + 0 \\[5pt] &= -4e^x\csc x + 4e^x\csc x \cot x \\[5pt] &= -4e^x\csc x(1 - \cot x) \end{align*}

Now, we substitute $x =\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and evaluate the slope $m{:}$

\begin{align*} m=g'(\dfrac{\pi}{2}) &= -4e^{\pi/2}\csc\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\left(1 - \cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\right) \\[5pt] &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ -4e^{\pi/2}} \end{align*}
